questions.question: Ishan starts from Point Y and drives 21 km towards the north. He then takes a left turn, drives 42 km, turns left and drives 41 km. He then takes a right turn and drives 17 km. He takes a right turn, drives 59 km. He then turns right, drives 18 km, turns right and drives 39 km to stop at Point Z. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point Y again? (All turns are 90-degree turns only unless specified.)
questions.solution:
Given:

Ishan starts from Point Y and drives 21 km towards the north.

He then takes a left turn, drives 42 km, turns left and drives 41 km.

He then takes a right turn and drives 17 km.

He takes a right turn, drives 59 km.

He then turns right, drives 18 km, turns right and drives 39 km to stop at Point Z. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a3b1aeafedf61cc8005ca408e528364a6a47223f3e07d4adf67d8f6da98add7a.png] 

Thus, Ishan should drive 41 km (42 km + 17 km - 18 km) in the east direction in order to reach Point Y again.​

Hence, "Option 1" is the correct answer.

questions.question: A, B, C, D, E, F, and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Only two people sit between D and F when counted from the left of F. E sits third to the left of G. A sits to the immediate right of G. A sits second to the left of D. B is an immediate neighbour of E. How many people sit between C and F when counted from the left of C?
questions.solution:
Given: A, B, C, D, E, F, and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre.

1) Only two people sit between D and F when counted from the left of F.

2) A sits second to the left of D. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/94aba44ba7ba0346e0a1b42127e81ff6412f34e1e2372dc68a2f2aba39f3675a.png] 

3) E sits third to the left of G.

4) B is an immediate neighbour of E. 

After positioning B, G and E only one position is left which will be occupied by the only person left i.e. C.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cae682b599d7351aad0bc41ee5c31d9450e4c8a32e0c9736ac75319562774a88.png] 

Thus, two people sit between C and F when counted from the left of C.

Hence, "Option 2" is the correct answer.

questions.question: Sujay ranked 29th from the top and 59th from the bottom in his class. How many students are there in his class?
questions.solution:
Given: Sujay ranked 29th from the top and 59th from the bottom in his class. 

Sujay's rank from the top = 29th

Sujay's rank from the bottom = 59th 

Total number of students = Sujay's rank from the top + Sujay's rank from the bottom - 1

= 29 + 59 - 1 → 87

Hence, "Option 3" is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

All sweater are jacket.

All sweater are coat.

All coat are blazer.

Conclusions:

(I) All sweater are blazer.

(II) Some coat are jacket.
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/429aba673c2c7d6c310d94686fb3d2c2bdd12e5cbab27ef6fa02c6c8a6dc602c.png] 

Conclusions:

(I) All sweater are blazer → Follow (As all sweater are coat and all coat are blazer. As whole sweater comes in coat which whole comes in blazer, therefore it is true)

(II) Some coat are jacket → Follow (As all sweater are jacket and all sweater are coat. As whole sweater comes in coats and jacket, therefore it is true)

∴ Here, Both conclusions (I) and (II) follow.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".
